bad.title: Four set widths, nothing else
bad.text: 60, 90, 120 or 180 cm. None is 105 cm.

bad.title: The only way on is a wrong size
bad.text: People give up, or buy a blind that doesn’t fit.

good.title: Custom… at the end of the list
good.text: The common widths stay one click away, and odd sizes still have a way in.

good.title: Type the width you measured
good.text: No need to round it to a size on the list.

good.title: The limits and the rounding, up front
good.text: Type 104.6 or 400, and it says what it changed.

bad.title: Lossless is gray, with no reason
bad.text: Clicking it does nothing, so people can’t tell if it’s broken or locked.

bad.title: An option that can never apply
bad.text: Dolby Atmos adds a second dead end that no plan will ever open.

good.title: The reason sits under Lossless
good.text: “Needs the Premium plan” tells people what it takes, in plain words.

good.title: See plans is the next step
good.text: People who want Lossless can go straight to the upgrade.

good.title: Each choice says what it costs
good.text: About 3 or 7 MB per song makes the trade-off concrete.

bad.title: No hint under Username
bad.text: Nothing says a space won’t work, so people type their full name.

bad.title: The rule arrives as a rejection
bad.text: People learn it only after a wasted try, then have to guess again.
bad.wait: Type Ana Silva and press Save to see this.

good.title: The rule, before the first try
good.text: Lowercase letters, numbers and dots, 3 to 20 characters. People shape the name to fit.

good.title: Saved on the first try
good.text: Type ana.silva and Save reports “Tries: 1”.
good.wait: Type ana.silva and press Save to see this.

bad.title: The list offers up to 30
bad.text: Nights 29 and 30 look bookable, so people pick them.

bad.title: The help text promises 31
bad.text: A third number, and none of them match the real limit.

bad.title: Refused at the very end
bad.text: The 28-night limit shows up only after people press Book.
bad.wait: Pick 30 and press Book to see this.

good.title: The list stops at 28
good.text: People can’t pick a stay the check would refuse.

good.title: The help text says 28 too
good.text: What people read matches what they can pick.

good.title: One rule feeds all three
good.text: Change the limit once, and the list, text and check move together.

bad.title: The comma in 5,5 is dropped
bad.text: Written the European way, 5.5 kg becomes 55 kg.

bad.title: The price is the only clue
bad.text: $86.50 instead of $12.25, and nothing says why.

good.title: A comma works as a decimal point
good.text: 5,5 and 5.5 mean the same, and 500 g works too.

good.title: The reading, in words
good.text: “Read as 5.5 kg.” shows before people pay, so a wrong guess is caught.

good.title: A price that matches the parcel
good.text: $12.25 for 5.5 kg, with no surprise at checkout.

bad.title: “7” could be morning or evening
bad.text: Dinner with Ana is almost surely 7 pm, but the field never asks.

bad.title: Dinner lands at 7:00 am
bad.text: Nothing flags the guess, so people may only notice on Friday.
bad.wait: Type 7 and press Add to see this.

good.title: Asks only when it’s two-way
good.text: 7:00 am and 7:00 pm, each one click away.
good.wait: Type 7 and press Add to see this.

good.title: “7pm” goes straight in
good.text: No question when there’s only one reading.
good.wait: Type 7pm and press Add to see this.

bad.title: Skip to wants mm:ss only
bad.text: 12m 30s is refused, though that’s how people say it.

bad.title: Sleep timer wants plain minutes
bad.text: 1h fails here, and so does the 12:30 that Skip to wanted.

good.title: Skip to takes the common formats
good.text: 12:30, 12m 30s and 45 min all work.

good.title: Sleep timer reads the same ones
good.text: 1h works, and so does anything that worked in Skip to.

bad.title: 10 x 14 turns into 10 × 15
bad.text: The field rewrites the size, and no message says so.

bad.title: The order changes without a word
bad.text: Type 100 x 150, and it quietly orders 30 × 45 cm.

good.title: Tidies 10x15cm quietly
good.text: Spaces and “cm” get cleaned up without comment, since the size stays the same.

good.title: Names the change it made
good.text: It says it changed 10 × 14 to 10 × 15 cm, so people know what they’ll get.
good.wait: Type 10 x 14 and press Tab to see this.

good.title: Refuses a size it can’t print
good.text: 100 x 150 gets the 30 × 45 cm limit instead of a guess.
good.wait: Type 100 x 150 and press Tab to see this.

bad.title: No save status anywhere
bad.text: People can’t tell if the list is saved, so they don’t trust it.

bad.title: Offline lines vanish on reopen
bad.text: Add a line with Wi-Fi off, reopen, and it’s gone without a word.

good.title: “Saved” in the title bar
good.text: It sits where people already look, and updates after each edit.

good.title: Offline says so and keeps the work
good.text: It sends the changes once Wi-Fi is back.
good.wait: Turn Wi-Fi off to see this.

good.title: Nothing lost on reopen
good.text: Lines added offline are still there after Close and reopen.

bad.title: Saved, with nothing behind it
bad.text: The delete is saved a second later, and no older copy exists.

bad.title: The pencil story is gone
bad.text: No History and no undo, so people rewrite it from memory.
bad.wait: Press Delete paragraph to see this.

good.title: History right next to Saved
good.text: Every autosave becomes a version people can go back to.

good.title: Restore on each older version
good.text: The 10:02 version with 3 paragraphs brings the pencil story back.

bad.title: Tab 2 saves over Tab 1
bad.text: Its copy never saw Apples, so adding Coffee wipes Apples out.

bad.title: Apples drops off the saved list
bad.text: After both adds, only Coffee is saved, and nobody is told.

good.title: Tab 2 notices the clash
good.text: Nothing saves until people choose what to keep.
good.wait: Add an item in Tab 1, then in Tab 2, to see this.

good.title: Neither tab’s work is lost
good.text: Keep mine as a copy saves Coffee aside, and Apples stays in the list.
good.wait: Add an item in Tab 1, then in Tab 2, to see this.

bad.title: Asks even when nothing was lost
bad.text: A plain Close and reopen still offers to restore a draft.
bad.wait: Press Close and reopen to see this.

bad.title: Discard has no way back
bad.text: Once people learn to wave it away, a real lost draft goes with it.
bad.wait: Press Close and reopen to see this.

good.title: No prompt when nothing’s lost
good.text: After Close and reopen, it just says there’s nothing to recover.
good.wait: Press Close and reopen to see this.

good.title: Shows up after a real crash
good.text: It appears only when the draft differs from the save, so people read it.
good.wait: Type something and press Crash to see this.
